gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's Apex 300 solar ports top out at 2 × 1,200 W (12–60 V, 20 A each, from the manual). Even with both ports filled, at full rated output it takes 29,564 Wh ÷ 2,400 W = 12.3 sun-hours to replace one day of the average US home's use. The 1,000 W of panels in the store bundle would need 29.6 sun-hours. The unit's own ~20 W idle draw also costs about 480 Wh a day.
standout_why: I compared against watthourlab.com/home-backup/transfer-switch-basics (cited). It lists solar-input totals (F3800 Plus 3,200 W, DELTA Pro 3 2,600 W) and 240 V outlet amps. It has no runtime or recharge arithmetic, no idle-draw figure, no per-port voltage or current limits, and no BLUETTI Apex 300. ChatGPT's own answer gives a battery runtime calculator (20 kWh against 30 kWh a day) and says only that 'solar panels must generate enough energy to replenish' it, with no numbers. I could not open popularmechanics.com, the other cited page, because the fetch was blocked. So I can't rule out that it has some of this, which is why the score is 2 and not 3. The finding is new and practical, but it doesn't rule out the kit. It sets expectations: this kit can back up chosen circuits but cannot run a whole average house on solar alone.
kit_items: Power station + expansion batteries: BLUETTI Apex 300 + 2× B300K (8,294.4 Wh, 3,840 W, 120/240 V). The store's own bundle with 2× 500 W panels keeps it to one cart. 8,294.4 Wh ÷ 1,232 W (average US home draw) = 6.7 h of whole-house use, so it suits chosen essential circuits, not the whole house.

Solar: 2× BLUETTI 500 W panels (SORA 500) included in that bundle, one per XT60 DC port. 1,000 W fits under the 2 × 1,200 W port limit. 8,294.4 Wh ÷ 1,000 W = 8.3 h of full-rated sun to refill from empty.
Home connection: BLUETTI Apex 300 Home Integration Kit (single Apex 300 version) feeds selected home circuits during an outage. It needs an electrician to install.
Optional upgrade for faster solar refill: BLUETTI SolarX 4K, which BLUETTI requires for its '4,000 W solar input' claim.
